**India**



- A formulation that is based on traditional Ayurvedic knowledge is excluded from patentability under Section 3(p) of the Indian Patents Act, which states that an invention that is, in effect, traditional knowledge is not an invention. [1]

- If the formulation is merely a mixture of known Ayurvedic ingredients without any enhancement of efficacy, it is also excluded under Section 3(e), which bars a substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components. [1]

- Guidelines for processing patent applications relating to traditional knowledge require that any claim involving a known Ayurvedic formulation be examined for novelty and inventive step; if the formulation is disclosed in the Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) or otherwise known in the public domain, it cannot be patented. [4] [5]



**Sources**
